mainProgression.description: Andy Summers transformed a standard 1950s doo-wop progression into a haunting new wave masterpiece by systematically adding major 9th intervals to every single chord, stretching across five frets under continuous palm muting.

sectionProgressions.description: Hypnotic, unending sixteenth-note arpeggiated cycle requiring immense fret-hand finger stretch and endurance

harmonicFunction: Abadd9 (I) - Luminous tonic chord made bittersweet by the ringing Bb major 9th
Fmadd9 (vi) - Submediant chord introducing somber romantic obsession with its G natural 9th
Dbadd9 (IV) - Subdominant chord expanding the sonic spectrum with Eb major 9th
Ebadd9 (V) - Dominant chord providing disciplined structural turnaround without unresolved cliché
E (bVI) - Borrowed chromatic chord in the bridge creating striking emotional disruption

techniques.name: Wide-Stretch Add9 Finger Geometry
techniques.description: Fretting demanding five-fret stretches across strings 6, 5, 4, and 3 while maintaining pristine note clarity and preventing fret-hand muscular strain

notes: Keep your fret-hand thumb positioned strictly in the middle of the back of the neck, never wrapping over the top
Arch fingers 1, 3, and 4 so they strike strings at a perpendicular 90-degree angle
Use index finger on the root (fret 4 on low E), ring finger on 5th (fret 6 on A), and pinky on 9th (fret 8 on D)
Relax fret-hand tension between chord changes to avoid tendonitis and cramping
sequence: Fret Ab on fret 4 (string 6) with index finger
Fret Eb on fret 6 (string 5) with ring finger
Fret Bb on fret 8 (string 4) with pinky finger
Fret C on fret 5 (string 3) with middle finger
tips: Warm up with gentle finger-stretching exercises before tackling this piece
If the five-fret stretch causes discomfort, use a capo on the 1st or 2nd fret initially to reduce fret distance
Lower your guitar strap slightly or adjust neck angle upward to ensure comfortable wrist alignment

techniques.name: Linear Telecaster Palm Muting
techniques.description: Applying the heel of the pick hand lightly across the bridge saddles to damp every individual sixteenth note into a clean, clockwork acoustic pulse

notes: Rest the fleshy outer heel of the pick hand directly over the bridge saddles
Ensure every string receives equal muting so lower strings don't boom over higher strings
Use small, mechanical downstrokes or alternate picking to emulate a drum machine
Never let notes bleed into one another; maintain strict staccato note isolation
sequence: Pick string 6 (root) with light percussive snap
Pick string 5, string 4, and string 3 in strict sixteenth-note timing
Reverse back down string 4 to complete the 8-note arpeggio cell
tips: Andy Summers utilized a 1961 Fender Telecaster Custom with an onboard preamp for crystalline cut
Add an analog compressor (Boss CS-2 or MXR Dyna Comp) to even out individual note volume
Engage an analog chorus/flanger pedal with slow depth to achieve the signature watery 1983 shimmer

sections.name: Intro Clockwork Arpeggio Setup
sections.description: The immortal guitar figure begins in solo isolation: Andy Summers' Telecaster chimes with shimmering chorus and mechanical palm-muted precision at 117 BPM.
notes: Strict palm muting on the bridge
Let the high major 9th interval (Bb) ring crisp and defined
Smooth fret-hand slide down to the Fmadd9 voicing
Maintain absolute rhythmic consistency like a metronome

sections.name: Verse 1 Hypnotic Staccato Drive
sections.description: Sting's cool, restrained vocal enters over Stewart Copeland's crisp hi-hat and Summers' unyielding arpeggiated cycle.
notes: Shift to Dbadd9 on the 5th string (fret 4 of A string)
Slide up two frets to Ebadd9 on fret 6 of A string
Keep pick attack even across all four strings
Focus on fret-hand thumb relaxation during shifts

sections.name: Chorus Melodic Expansion
sections.description: 'Oh, can't you see, you belong to me...' - the emotional peak of the song as the progression shifts starting on the Dbadd9 chord.
sections.progression: Dbadd9 - Abadd9 - Ebadd9 - Fmadd9 - Dbadd9 - Abadd9 - Ebadd9
notes: Slightly relax palm muting for subtle dynamic blooming
Bass guitar supports with deep, warm pedal tones
High vocal harmonies blend with guitar overtones
Tight turnaround on Ebadd9 back to the verse groove

sections.name: Bridge Chromatic Modulation
sections.description: 'Since you've gone I've been lost without a trace...' - abrupt key shift to E major creating dark, obsessive emotional intensity before resolving through Eb.
sections.progression: E - F# - B - E - F# - Eb
notes: Switch to open/barre chord voicings in E major
Intensify pick-hand downstrokes as harmonic tension builds
The climactic Eb major chord acts as the dominant V leading home to Ab
Crisp return to signature muted arpeggios on beat 1

sections.name: Outro Vamp & Hypnotic Fade
sections.description: Continuous cyclical repetition of the Abadd9 and Fmadd9 arpeggios fading into infinity while Sting improvises soaring vocal counter-melodies.
notes: Focus on breathing and pick-hand muscle memory
Maintain unwavering staccato muting to the very end
Subtle chorus pedal sweeps expand the stereo field
Gradual studio fader decay

guitar.pickup: Bridge single-coil for biting articulation, or middle position for crystalline shimmer

amp.recommended: Roland JC-120 Jazz Chorus or Marshall 1959 Plexi set clean

effects.other: Boss CE-1 / CE-2 Chorus or Electro-Harmonix Electric Mistress Flanger, paired with Boss CS-2 Compressor

beginner.title: Basic Triad Progression
steps: Learn standard Ab, Fm, Db, and Eb major/minor barre chords
Practice transitioning between chords at 117 BPM
Establish palm muting technique on downstrokes

intermediate.title: The Add9 Chord Shapes & Muting
steps: Practice the five-fret finger stretch using a capo initially
Master the Abadd9 and Fmadd9 arpeggiation patterns
Lock in strict sixteenth-note palm muting without choking notes

advanced.title: Endurance, Bridge Modulation & Full Performance
steps: Perform the entire 4-minute song without fret-hand fatigue
Execute the dramatic chromatic key shift in the bridge smoothly
Replicate Andy Summers' studio tone with compressor, chorus, and plate reverb

commonMistakes: Wrapping the fret-hand thumb around the neck, which collapses the finger arch and makes the five-fret stretch impossible
Pressing too hard with the pick-hand palm, deadening the note tone into a thud instead of a ringing chime
Tensing the fret hand forearm, leading to rapid muscle exhaustion and strain
Rushing the tempo during chord shifts instead of maintaining clockwork 117 BPM timekeeping
practiceRoutine: 5 mins: Gentle fret-hand finger stretching and spider warmup exercises
10 mins: Slow arpeggiation of Abadd9 at 70, 90, and 117 BPM
10 mins: Chord transition drills between Abadd9 and Fmadd9
10 mins: Bridge modulation study focusing on the altered Eb turnaround
focusAreas: Fret-hand thumb positioning and finger arch geometry
Consistent bridge palm muting across all strings
Muscular endurance and relaxation during repetitive cycles
metronomeWork: Begin at 70 BPM to ensure every note in the add9 voicing rings cleanly without buzzing
Advance by 4 BPM only when you can complete 8 consecutive measures without hand tension
Practice with metronome clicking on sixteenth-note subdivisions to develop unwavering precision
